articleTitle: A Review on the Applications of Machine Learning Algorithms for Mental Stress Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: Stress, a widespread issue affecting both individual well-being and societal productivity, has attracted significant research interest. Defined as a state of mental or emotional strain, stress arises from various factors such as work, relationships, and health concerns, manifesting physically, emotionally, and behaviorally. This paper provides a review of Machine Learning (ML) techniques to detect mental stress using physiological signals like ECG, GSR, and EEG. Through a review of existing studies, the paper highlights the progress made in this area and the challenges that remain, particularly concerning data quality, algorithm accuracy, and the practical deployment of stress monitoring devices. The study underscores the potential for real-time monitoring and personalized interventions, especially in daily activities. Future research should focus on enhancing model robustness, integrating multiple data sources, and addressing real-world applicability. This paper emphasizes the importance of early stress identification and personalized treatment to improve mental health outcomes

articleTitle: A Mathematical Model for Transformation Matrices in Ultrasound Probe Positioning and Orientation
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: This paper produces a novel approach to determine the position and orientation of an ultrasound probe in 3D space. The probe carries an orthogonal set of laser lines that project onto two orthogonal planes, and a pair of high-resolution Pi cameras are positioned orthogonal to each other while facing the two planes to capture the laser lines appearing on these planes. This approach is unlike traditional methods that guide the placement of a probe based on operator skill. Basic functions of the system work with image processing algorithms, so the endpoint of the two laser lines are found on the processed images and thus the transformation matrix that describes probe position and orientation is calculated in the predefined coordinate system. Parameters of translation and rotation are derived from this matrix, where multiple iterations of the transformation are performed in real time to minimize the error. Using this methodology brings in a strong solution for positioning the probe more precisely in a 3D space, which is a huge step forward compared to traditional methods which lack computational support. The results demonstrate the ability of this method to accurately determine the initial position and orientation of the probe. Echocardiogram imaging systems guided by artificial intelligence depend on very accurate probe position and orientation information to improve their capacity to offer real-time, patient-specific recommendations on the probe position giving out the highest quality images.

articleTitle: AI’s Corrective Feedback vs. Traditional Recasts: which fosters better grammar accuracy?
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: This paper discusses how effective ChatGPT, developed by OpenAI, is likely to be compared to traditional corrective recasts in teaching English grammar to engineering undergraduates. With the rise of digital communication, a generation of learners for whom traditional methods seem to be less effective has emerged. This research contrasts the effects of ChatGPT's corrective feedback versus conventional teacher-led corrective recasts on grammatical proficiency among students, especially in subject-verb agreement and accuracy in tenses. 90 engineering students were divided into two groups ᅳ one with the traditional approach to instruction and another using ChatGPT to practice grammar. Pre- and post-assessment tests were administered to the participants to measure improvements in grammar proficiency. Statistical analysis, using paired t-tests, indicated that both groups improved significantly, with the ChatGPT-assisted group showing more improvement in proficiency compared to the traditional approach. Another independent sample t-test confirmed that the AI-led feedback group had a significantly larger mean improvement in grammar proficiency compared to the traditional instruction group. The results of this study demonstrate that ChatGPT provides more effective corrective feedback to engineering students with varying levels of proficiency in subject-verb agreement and tenses usage, suggesting potential benefits for language education through integration with AI.

articleTitle: Comparing Neural Networks In Human Brains And AI Systems With Focus On Genetics And Experiential Differences
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: This research investigates the comparative dynamics between human intelligence and artificial intelligence (AI), focusing on the parallels between the human brain and microprocessors. It begins by exploring the foundational principles of cognition and computing, emphasizing how microprocessors have drawn inspiration from the brain's complexity. Despite their distinct compositions, both the human brain and microprocessors exhibit similarities in information processing, storage, and execution, mirroring each other’s mechanisms through electrical impulses and interconnected components. The study reviews literature on AI working, the influence of genetics and environmental factors on human behavior, and the capabilities of neural networks. The research underscores the significance of genetic inheritance, its effect on neural networks in humans along with the environmental experiences in shaping behavior and personality. The findings contribute to a deeper understanding of both biological and artificial intelligence. Ultimately, this study demonstrates the potential for leveraging insights from both domains to enhance human well-being and technological progress.

articleTitle: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence for Effective Assessment and Evaluation in Education: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: Assessment and evaluation are indeed chief ways through which student learning can be measured, downtrend areas of their performances perfected, and instructional strategies shaped. The incorporation of Artificial Intelligence into these processes may completely revolutionize traditional approaches: more accurate, efficient, and individualized assessment. The in-depth review herein makes a case for how AI technologies are potentially going to revolutionize educational assessment and evaluation. Some of the salient findings that come out are that AI can provide instant feedback; it is "highly accurate in assessments using advanced data analytics"; it facilitates personalized learning experiences, meeting the requirements of each student. The review also looks at a number of challenges and ethical concerns concerning AI adoption in education, and provides insights into how these technologies can be implemented effectively and responsibly to improve educational outcomes.

articleTitle: Development of Deep Learning Model for Detection of Abdominal Diseases using Radiological Images
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: As the abdominal and chest injuries are high morbidity and mortality around the globe, these pose an acute challenge in emergency care. Current data from recently released sources indicate that more than half of the patients visiting ER and also being admitted into hospital account for trauma; and the burden of both abdominal and chest injuries is quite high. Imaging plays an important role in diagnosis and treatment planning in the management of abdominal and chest injuries. The most widely practiced modality is radiograph imaging simply because it produces quality and easy results. Improving Automated pathology object detection of things in radiographs with deep learning algorithms promises much for the precision of diagnosis and optimization in health care. This paper discusses and provides a very detailed review of optimized CNNs, primarily ResNet18, ResNet34, along with a custom-built neural network for the identification of disease from X-ray pictures. Such models are trained and validated to reach excellent sensitivity and specificity on a wide variety of diseases by using the annotated RSNA 2023 dataset by professionals in radiology. It extended the scope of earlier research in this field by looking at other imaging conditions and diseases as well. This puts its contribution into the larger, ongoing discussion of AI in radiology. The results of this study help to contribute to the thesis that the promise of deep learning in radiological diagnosis is substantial, and it could be used to better enhance patient outcomes in the practice of emergency radiology.

articleTitle: Transformative Trends in Diabetes Care: An Analysis of AI-Enhanced Predictive Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: This article examines the ever-changing environment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in diabetes treatment. It investigates its existing uses, future developments, and the complex interaction of technology innovation, regulatory concerns, and ethical imperatives. AI is transforming diabetes management, from predictive analytics to tailored treatment regimens, by providing real-time information, increasing patient empowerment, and contributing to proactive, individualized care. The developing legal framework and emerging standards work to assure responsible AI technology development and deployment, addressing algorithmic biases and data privacy issues. The study forecasts future developments in the industry, imagining a collaborative future in which AI, seamlessly linked with other technology, augments healthcare professionals' competence and empowers people with diabetes. This investigation is guided by a synthesis of technological and ethical issues, highlighting the importance of inclusion, accessibility, and a harmonious human-AI relationship to advance the future of diabetes treatment toward better results and greater patient well-being

articleTitle: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Forensic Odontology: A Narrative Review of the Current Applications, Associated Challenges, and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: This article explores the application of artificial intelligence (AI) in the field of forensic dentistry to improve accuracy for human/object identification, minimize the errors, and enhance the productivity of forensic values as in gender determination, bite mark analysis, age estimation, and human identification. Convolutional neural networks (CNN's) and other AI algorithms outperformed traditional approaches in these values. However, difficulties such as data-set limits and ethical issues persist. This review paper emphasis the importance of collaboration across disciplines and more diverse data-sets in order to incorporate AI into forensic dentistry techniques. To fully realize AI's promise in the health-care sector, more research should address these issues.

articleTitle: A Meta-Analysis of AI in Fraud Detection: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Different Algorithms and Data Sources

articleTitle: Comprehensive Overview of Gas and Bio-Sensors Enabling Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: Gas and biosensors are crucial in the modern healthcare system, enabling non-invasive monitoring and diagnosis of various medical conditions. These sensors are used in various applications, including smart home health monitoring devices and critical care units. Common non-imaging sensor types include gas or VOC sensors, diagnostic ECG sensors, blood glucose sensors, pulse oximeters, blood pressure sensors, body temperature sensors, EEG sensors, accelerometers, and imaging sensors like X-rays, MRIs, CT scans, and ultrasounds. Healthcare-related sensors offer numerous advantages, including diagnosing and treating medical conditions, monitoring vital signs, enabling remote patient monitoring, personalized healthcare, and early detection and prevention. However, issues like data accessibility, privacy, comfort, security, and accuracy must be considered when installing sensors in homes. Efficient data sharing and analysis require devices, sensors, and platforms to communicate effectively. Real-time data processing is essential for prompt diagnosis and intervention. In this article, we have put it briefly: medical sensors are transforming the way we track, identify, and manage adverse health conditions.

articleTitle: The Future of Driving: A Review on the Combination of Artificial Intelligence and Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: The convergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Vehicles (AV) are poised to revolutionize the automotive industry, offering safer, more efficient, and sustainable transportation solutions. This review article explores the current state of AVs, role of AI in AV, challenges and hurdles, Real world applications & development, its critical technological components, and their impact on society. This paper presents a wide array of applications of AI in AV, elaborating on the way complex sensor fusion, computer vision, and Machine Learning (ML) algorithms makes AVs perceive their surroundings, form critical opinions, and carry out accurate motions. AI is making real time interpretations of great quantities of data which are paving the way for safer and more effective navigation under a diversity of traffic circumstances, from sensor fusion to decision-making algorithms. The next section of this paper elaborates on the role of AI in the field of AV in perceiving, planning, and navigating through real world environment, while also talking about issues of integration and ethics. This paper further identifies its social, economic, and environmental consequences, resulting from mass use of AV. This article discusses the latest developments and opportunities in the regulatory environment, gives an overview of how AV define transportation in the near future. This paper also explores the levels of autonomy of AVs as defined by the Society of Automotive Engineers (SAE) and defines the process from driver assistance to full automation. It examines the ethical and technical considerations arising at each instant and emphasizes the key role AI continues to play in providing more autonomy while preserving security and dependability.

articleTitle: VTherapy: Deep Learning-based Hand Rehabilitation System
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: In this research, we introduce a virtual hand rehabilitation system, VTherapy, that amalgamates a deep learning model with a Flask web application, aimed at enhancing post-injury hand therapy at home. Our system leverages a deep learning architecture combining ResNeXt50's feature extraction with LSTM's sequential data analysis for precise hand gesture recognition. This methodology is augmented by the Dynamic Time Warping algorithm to accurately assess the similarity between the patient’s exercise video sequences and the reference exercise video. This approach not only democratizes access to effective hand rehabilitation by offering a cost-efficient, home-based solution but also promotes patient autonomy and engagement through interactive feedback mechanisms. The salient features of this system include an exercise performance tracker with goal setting, a real-time interactive rule-based chatbot trained using a neural network, and appointment scheduler to connect patients with physiotherapists. A dedicated SQLite database underpins the system by recording every exercise instance, facilitating feedback-driven progress tracking. The confluence of cutting-edge deep learning with user-friendly web technology presents a paradigm shift in rehabilitative care, potentially transforming the landscape of home-based physiotherapy for patients recovering from hand injuries.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Security Impact of Face Recognition and IoT-Enabled Blockchain on Electronic Voting Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: Electronic voting has seen persistent security and privacy issues preventing its widespread adoption and success. This research introduces a robust framework that leverages advanced hashing, encryption techniques with blockchain technology which enhance the security of voting transaction and authenticity of voter data. India, which is world's largest democracy, faces electoral challenges such as fake voting and tampering with Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs). Addressing these issues biometric-based voting system that verifies voter identity through fingerprint authentication is the suggested. This system ensures that each voter casts only one authenticated vote, adhering to the principle of "Single voter, Single authenticated vote". Proposed biometric prototype for voting machine and its integration with the Aadhar database can be maintained by the help of Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI). This advancement can significantly enhance the device's application at the national level, making it feasible for use in elections across the country. By implementing this biometric-based voting system, efficiency improvement and by implementing blockchain transparency, security, and efficiency achieved. The proposed framework strengthens the electoral process's integrity, transparent, secure, and efficient voting system.

articleTitle: Enhanced E-Commerce Demand Prediction through Ensemble Models and Optuna-Based Hyperparameter Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: The fast growth of e-commerce has made sophisticated prediction models necessary to precisely forecast demand and maximize inventory control developed. In a very competitive industry, effective demand forecasting is absolutely essential for lowering costs, avoiding waste, and raising customer satisfaction. This work presents a complex ensemble-based method combining Random Forest models with hyperparameter optimization enabled by Optuna with LightGBM and XGBoost. This approach guarantees best performance via exact tweaking and makes use of the features of every model. Rigorously evaluated on actual e-commerce data, our suggested model shows a notable lower MAPE than independent models. With a MAPE of 0.0341, the ensemble model specifically outperformed LightGBM (0.0344), XGBoost (0.00336), and Random Forest (0.0358) by roughly 2–5%. This development emphasizes how well combined ensemble learning with hyperparameter optimization increases predicted accuracy. Furthermore, our method provides scalability and adaptability, which qualifies for many e-commerce situations from high-dimensional data settings to perishable items. This study shows that the suggested ensemble model offers a strong, adaptable demand forecasting solution for e-commerce and increases forecast accuracy, therefore opening the path for more effective and data-driven decision-making procedures.

articleTitle: A Review of Social Media Sentiment Analysis Using Machine Learning To Enhance Stock Market Prediction

abstract: Predicting stock prices is a critical financial activity that is frequently impacted by sentiment analysis, machine learning, and data mining approaches. This examination looks at a variety of stock price prediction methods, including artificial neural networks, graph-based approaches, time series analysis, and classic machine learning techniques such as Support Vector Machine, K-Nearest Neighbor, and Random Forest. The article assesses the problems and efficacy of various methodologies, including a thorough examination of sentiment analysis in social media to enhance stock market predictions. By examining multiple research, this study provides a complete evaluation of various prediction algorithms and reveals their shortcomings, such as overfitting, non-stationary data, and the complexity of financial transactions. It helps academics and practitioners construct more accurate and dependable stock forecasting models by merging financial data with sentiment analysis. The study also discusses rising trends and new potential for further study, especially hybrid models and advanced deep learning approaches to improve the accuracy of stock forecasts.

articleTitle: Ethical Considerations in AI-Driven Supply Chain Management: A Review of Emerging Trends and Challenges

articleTitle: A Novel Hybrid Model for Efficient Prediction of Diabetes Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: Diabetes mellitus, a long-term metabolic disease marked by elevated blood glucose levels, has a substantial negative impact on public health worldwide. Accurate prediction is essential for effective diabetes treatment due to its increasing prevalence. Machine Learning (ML) addresses the issues of this chronic metabolic condition, which provides a promising answer by enabling individualized therapies. This paper presents a comprehensive study on diabetes prediction using ML techniques, focusing on a hybrid approach stacked ensemble models. The research employs the Indian Pima dataset from Kaggle. The primary objective is to assess various ML models with and without preprocessing techniques. Preprocessing involves data cleaning, normalization, and feature engineering to enhance predictive accuracy. Overall, the results underscore the importance of preprocessing in improving predictive performance and highlight the efficacy of hybrid ensemble techniques in diabetic prediction tasks. Moreover, the hybrid approach utilizes a stacked ensemble comprising Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) as base models and Logistic Regression as a meta-model. The hybrid approach achieves superior performance compared to individual models with 95.1% accuracy. This methodology effectively combines the strengths of diverse algorithms, mitigating their weaknesses and yielding more robust predictions. It provides substantial benefits by integrating ML algorithms, statistical techniques, and expert knowledge.

articleTitle: Multimodal Machine Learning for Early Detection of Autism in Children: Integrating Gestures and Mood Analysis

abstract: autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is characterized by neurological disorders and challenges with interpersonal communication, communication, and schedule behaviour. Early distinguishing proof of ASD is vital to optimize the intervention and progress long-term results. This paper analyses the potential of numerous machine learning procedures for early location of ASD in children. We propose a novel approach that combines gesture assessment with cognitive evaluation to capture a comprehensive picture of a child’s behaviour. Side effect analysis will focus on highlights such as body language, hand movements, and eye contact, which can give profitable bits of knowledge into the social and communication designs of children with ASD. Therapy will utilize facial expressions, tone of voice, and body language to survey a child’s emotional state. The proposed strategy can be connected in different situations, such as during routine testing or through a portable application. Early and precise conclusion can clear the way for convenient intervention and back for children with ASD, eventually driving to positive long-term results.

articleTitle: Maize Leaf Disease Detection Using a Transfer Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: Maize, as a staple food crop, plays a crucial role in global food security. However, its production is significantly threatened by various diseases affecting maize leaves. In order to reduce yield expenses, early identification and treatment of certain diseases become crucial. In this work, we suggest a transfer learning model for the diagnosis of maize crop leaf disease. In this paper used pre-trained models such as MobileNet and MobileNetV2, fine-tuned on a dataset comprising images of maize leaves with different diseases. The final results demonstrate the effectiveness of transfer learning, with the suggested model achieving an accuracy of 96.00% on the PlantVillage dataset, outperforming existing methods. This approach shows great potential for practical application in agriculture, enabling early and accurate detection of maize leaf diseases for timely manner and enhancing the crop yield.

articleTitle: Advancements in Video Content Analysis using Machine Learning for Educational Applications: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: The video analysis is one of the ever-growing field in research. The introduction of new technology and use of video lectures in education has opened new possible ways of using videos. Video lecture have become preferred choice for E-learning platforms which includes distance education, Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCS), universities courses. Government of India has launched the new initiatives for E-learning such as Swayam, National Programme for Technology Enhanced Learning (NPTEL) online courses which are based on the video-based content delivery. Only on YouTube every day around 400 billion videos are watched and 300 hrs. of videos are uploaded every minute. The video has been the central part of the many researchers. It has been used in the research of Facial Expression Recognition, indexing of the video, analyzing the contents of video with the help of metadata of video, transcripts, course material. There are attempts to generate a heatmap of a video based on the number of times a particular frame is visited by user; some approaches even combine heatmap generation with eye gaze tracking of student using eye tracking tools to identify the highest and lowest watched frames in the video. The present work in the area of content-based video analysis have focused on finding the topic of video, key frames in video, locating the object and finding its presence in all past and future frame of video. The paper discusses the key development in the area of video content analysis to help improve the quality of learning.

articleTitle: Steel Plate Defect Detection and Classification using Light weight MobileNetV2 Model
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: In the steel manufacturing sector, automated surface flaw identification is critical to manufacturing quality monitoring. Unfortunately, due to its poor accuracy and sluggish operation, the manual approach is not suitable to be utilized on a manufacturing process. The prevalent AI-based technique now in use suffers from poor accuracy as well, while there remains much space for development. This paper presents a comparative analysis of various classifiers for steel plate defect detection, focusing on the performance of Random Forest, Xgboost, MobileNet, and MobileNetV2. The Random Forest classifier achieved an accuracy of 46.66%, while Xgboost performed slightly lower at 43.33%. A combination of MobileNet for feature extraction and Xgboost for classification resulted in a notable improvement, reaching an accuracy of 60.00%. However, the most impressive performance was observed with MobileNetV2, which achieved an accuracy of 83.00%, significantly outperforming the other models. This study demonstrates the superior efficacy of MobileNetV2 for detecting defects in steel plates, highlighting its potential for industrial applications. The paper also discusses the future scope of enhancing defect detection through advanced deep learning techniques and real-time implementation.

articleTitle: Systematic Review of Recent ChatGPT updates on Reporting of Radiology Cases with Reference to Magnetic Resonance Imaging of the Lumbar Spine
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: This systematic review aims to evaluate the recent advancements and applications of ChatGPT in reporting radiology cases, focusing on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the lumbar spine. The review adheres to the PRISMA guidelines and explores how artificial intelligence (AI) can improve the accuracy, efficiency, and consistency of radiology reports. A comprehensive literature search was conducted across databases such as PubMed, Scopus, and IEEE Xplore, covering articles published from January 2022 to September 2024. The inclusion criteria were studies that examined the use of ChatGPT or similar AI models in radiology reporting, specifically focusing on MRI of the lumbar spine. Studies not involving ChatGPT or AI, non-radiology-related studies, and articles not available in full text were excluded. Data extraction and synthesis were performed in line with PRISMA guidelines. A total of 18 studies met the inclusion criteria, with 12 focusing on MRI of the lumbar spine. The findings indicate that ChatGPT shows potential in standardizing radiology reports, improving diagnostic accuracy, and reducing the time needed for report generation. However, challenges such as the necessity for clinical context, risks of over-reliance on AI, and issues regarding the interpretability of AI outputs were noted. ChatGPT and similar AI models have considerable potential in radiology reporting, especially for lumbar spine MRI. However, careful implementation, continuous updates, and rigorous validation are crucial to ensure these tools enhance rather than replace the expertise of radiologists.

articleTitle: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Personalized Nutrition and Healthcare Management
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: AI is changing personalized nutrition and healthcare management by combining powerful data analytics, predictive technology, and machine learning. With the use of AI tailored nutrition if possible specific diet advice real time nutrient tracking meal plans all based off of an individual’s health information. Speaking of healthcare management, with the use of AI, the predictive analytics are better, the treatment strategies are more specific, and real time health monitoring and even virtual health help is possible. Although AI has a lot of potential in these fields, it also creates many problems, such as privacy issues, error rates, prejudice, and getting the system to fit in with the rest of the system. This article explores the current applications, advantages and drawbacks of AI in personalized nutrition and health care delivery and offers a comprehensive analysis of its impact as well as future trends.

articleTitle: AI and the Future of Work in Logistics: A Delphi Study on Workforce Transformation
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: AI being used in transportation is going to change the future of work by changing how people work together and how things are done. This Delphi study looks at how AI is changing transportation, focused on how it changes the work force and what the geopolitical effects are. This study combines ideas to shed light on how things are changing by carefully looking at the opinions of experts and predicted trends. When AI is used in transportation, big improvements are expected, such as more efficient operations, the ability to make predictions, and the ability to make decisions on its own. It is expected that these new ideas will make the supply chain more efficient, cut costs, and lower risks, making the whole system more flexible and strong. Along with these possibilities, though, there are worries about how AI will change established jobs and the need for more skills to fully use AI's potential. Key results show that experts agree on one thing: AI is the key to making all business tasks more efficient. One of the main benefits of AI is that it can automate boring chores like managing supplies, finding the best routes, and planning for future upkeep. Also, AI-powered data give you information in real time, which helps you make better decisions and adapt to changes in the market. The study finds important changes that need to happen in the workforce because of AI usage. It talks about the rise of new job categories, like AI system teachers, data scientists, and AI ethicists that need skills from a lot of different fields, like being good with technology and knowing a lot about the subject.

articleTitle: Advancing Malware Defense: A Hybrid Approach with Explainable Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: Malware detection and classification remain critical challenges in cybersecurity, necessitating advanced techniques for combating increasingly sophisticated threats. This paper presents a novel hybrid approach that leverages the power of explainable deep neural networks to enhance malware detection and classification accuracy while providing interpretable results. The proposed method combines static and dynamic analysis techniques to extract a comprehensive set of features from both executable files and runtime behaviors. These features are then processed using a custom-designed deep neural network architecture that incorporates attention mechanisms and interpretability layers. The model not only achieves high accuracy in detecting and classifying various malware families, but also offers explanations for its decisions, addressing the "black box" problem often associated with deep learning models. The experimental results demonstrated the effectiveness of this hybrid approach, showing significant improvements over traditional machine learning methods and baseline deep learning models. The explainable component of the system provides valuable insights into the specific characteristics and behaviors that contribute to malware identification, potentially aiding the development of more robust defense mechanisms. This research contributes to the field by offering a powerful, interpretable tool for malware analysis that can adapt to evolving threats while providing transparency in its decision-making process, thus bridging the gap between advanced AI techniques and practical cybersecurity applications.

articleTitle: A Review on How AI Helps in Treating Mental Illness
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: Mood rating scales, electronic health records (EHR), king data from brain imaging, and other medical applications innovative monitoring systems that could identify, anticipate, and categorize mental health disorders. It reviews and discusses how AI can support clinical practice while taking into account its existing limits. It treats and identifies disease. Through the use of the smart edge, the research is intended to assist physicians, researchers, and public health o detects a person's heart rate, level of happiness, mental health, and attempts at suicide in order to determine whether or not they may have mental officials in controlling and managing this condition. The number of cases of mental health concerns is currently at an all-time high, and it may rise much further in the near future The advancement of digital tools to identify emotions through patterns has applications in several mental health care domains such as diagnosis, monitoring, and detection. AI is being used in therapy to improve user experience and maximize individualized psychological state care through digital interventions, most notably internet and smartphone apps. Data-driven technologies, such as artificial intelligence, are used to build prediction and detection models for circumstances related to psychological states.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Role of Machine Learning and Satellite Image Processing in Predicting Deforestation
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: Loss of species, climate change, and ecosystem damage are all caused by cutting down trees, which is a major world environmental problem. Predicting when trees will be cut down is important for starting protection efforts at the right time. As a result, machine learning and picture processing from satellites have become useful and accurate ways to predict deforestation on a large scale. This research looks into how machine learning techniques and high-resolution satellite images can be used together to very accurately predict when forests will be cut down. Land cover changes over time can be seen in satellite pictures, which give us a lot of information about space. Advanced methods, like remote sensing and picture segmentation, can be used to process these photos and pull out important traits that show deforestation. Then, machine learning methods like Random Forests, Support Vector Machines, and Convolutional Neural Networks are used on these traits to model and predict trends of destruction. The study compares different machine learning models based on how accurate they are, how quickly they can be run, and how well they can work in different parts of the world. Integrating satellite picture processing with machine learning makes it possible to find out what causes trees to be cut down, like expanding farms, cutting, and urbanization. This makes it easier to come up with specific conservation plans. Using time-series satellite data lets us see how deforestation changes over time, which helps us understand how forest cover loss changes over time. Traditional methods are often limited by not having enough data from the ground and not being able to work over big areas. This method has a lot of benefits over those. The results show that using machine learning and satellite picture processing together can make very accurate predictions. This could be a useful tool for lawmakers and environmentalists. By making it easier to predict deforestation, this method encourages taking proactive steps to lessen its effects, eventually supporting global efforts to protect the environment and promote sustainable development.

articleTitle: Ethical Guidelines For Utilization of Artificial Intelligence In Healthcare: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: The key issue is to develop guidelines for Artificial Intelligence (AI) data protection that respect individual rights and further the general welfare. Where possible, AI systems have to minimize data of a personal nature to the absolute minimum, anonymize such data, and encrypt it in maintaining data security in accordance with regulations such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). AI systems need to follow the levels defined by the European Commission to achieve proper transparency and explain ability for building confidence and enabling proper ethical control. The present review article aims to bring ethical standard for AI utilization upfront. Additionally, the present article focus on uncovering ethical guidelines for maintaining standards for AI use. A thorough search approach was used to find relevant reviews of the literature for the assessment. Phases of the strategy included scanning several databases, evaluating publications, and choosing the most relevant research for review. This review examined electronic databases including PubMed, Science Direct, EMBASE, and Google Scholar. These databases were chosen to provide comprehensive coverage of relevant content. Making use of studies and reviews published between 2000 and 2024.

articleTitle: A Review on Soil Moisture Monitoring Methods using Satellite Images
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: Soil moisture is an important parameter in the hydrological cycle and an important component for agricultural production and prediction. The regular monitoring of soil moisture plays a big role in the prediction and management of crops and droughts in a region. Climate change has led to irregular patterns in rainfall and extreme weather conditions worldwide. This has led to the farmers taking extreme steps. The traditional method is the best method of measuring soil moisture, but it requires a lot of time and is labor-intensive. Therefore, satellite remote sensing provides an alternative approach to measuring soil moisture covering a large area within less time. The application of satellite remote sensing provides comparative results to traditional methods. This study provides a discussion on spectral indices obtained from satellite data for measuring soil moisture. The current study also provides insights about the applications, challenges, and advantages of using satellite remote sensing for monitoring of soil moisture using remote sensing datasets. The study may be helpful to farmers and government agencies for planning and management of crops and water preservation over the drought prone regions of India.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Models in Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: Modern society has placed more emphasis on well-being, focusing on better healthcare services at whatever cost. In the same vein, the healthcare system is working towards extending population health, improving treatment efficiency, and incrementally enhancing the experiences of patients. However, gaining and making sense of various complex biomedical data has been hard to get in the process of reforming healthcare. Modern biomedical research combines all types of information, from imaging to electronic health records, text, and sensor data, characterized by complexity, heterogeneity, and often ambiguity. Conventional statistical learning and data mining methods need a tremendous amount of feature engineering to extract meaningful insights and then build predictive or clustering models. However, these approaches are badly impeded due to the complex nature of the data and the lack of domain expertise. Deep learning is a disruptive technology that sidesteps conventional feature engineering and enables end-to-end learning directly from complex clinical data. Advanced architectures formulate a paramount data analysis at unprecedented scales and complexities, foretelling rapid, efficient, and precise insights. Deep learning integrated into health care holds several advantages in decision-making, mimicking human cognition. The multiple-layer architectures enable superior computational capabilities and refine vast amounts of previously untapped healthcare data. A capability like this would democratize expertise and let all health practitioners work right on the front lines while performing at a top specialist level. The sharing of deep learning models across different healthcare institutions could be done without the fear of leaking patient data, and this will open the way for a new generation of personalized medicine. However, the interpretability of models and other ethical concerns remain pertinent challenges. This review underlines deep learning as having a transformative role in health care by underscoring that it will help harness the vast biomedical data for the betterment of human health.

articleTitle: Hybrid VGG-SVM Framework for Melanoma Detection: Integrating GAN-Augmented Data and LIME Interpretability
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: Melanoma is a severe form of skin cancer that requires early detection for effective treatment. This study explores the use of advanced AI techniques to enhance the accuracy of melanoma diagnosis. We proposed a hybrid VGG-SVM model that incorporates GAN-based data augmentation to enhance the training process. Additionally, we used LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations) to gain insights into the model's decision-making. By training on large datasets of dermatoscopic images, our method aimed to detect subtle melanoma characteristics with high accuracy while maintaining explainability. The proposed VGG-SVM model, combined with LIME, achieved an accuracy, precision, and F1-score of 96%, surpassing previous state-of-the-art methods. This significant improvement in both accuracy and interpretability addresses a critical scientific gap in AI-assisted melanoma diagnosis, potentially enhancing early detection rates and clinical trust in AI systems. Our study demonstrates the potential of hybrid AI models in medical image analysis and highlights the importance of interpretability in clinical applications. Future work will focus on clinical validation and exploration of transfer learning techniques to further improve model performance across diverse patient populations.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cybersecurity and Threat Detection in Vehicular Ad-Hoc Networks (VANETs) using Blockchain and Fallback Policy
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: In the era of autonomous vehicles, Vehicular Ad-hoc networks (VANETs) are critical components of any Intelligent Transportation System (ITS). A Cyber security challenge makes VANETs vulnerable to various attacks, threats and challenges such as data manipulation, data tampering, denial-of-service attacks, privacy breaches and jamming of networks. This paper tries to explore the various cyber security challenges in VANETs and proposes an enhanced threat detection framework comprising deep-learning techniques and blockchain technology. The proposed framework aims to improve the detection accuracy of malicious activities and ensure secure communication among vehicles and infrastructure. Thus, saving lives and costs involved by a better fallback policy or contingency plan.

articleTitle: Medical Data Security and Privacy Preservation using Blockchain Technology Integrated with Healthcare 4.0 Standand:Current Method and Challanges
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: A significant hurdle for research conducted on cloud-based Healthcare 4.0 systems is guaranteeing patient privacy while dealing with biological data. Multimedia, numerical, and textual medical records are the three most common forms. Multimedia data includes imaging scans created by imaging technologies including computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and related methods. There are several privacy and security issues with sending biological multimedia data to medical authorities. There have been several proposals for how to protect the privacy of medical records throughout the last decade. The goal of these suggestions is to make sure that sensitive medical data is sent securely while yet protecting patient privacy. However, there is still a complicated research topic about how to achieve the best possible security and efficiency for medical data inside the Cloud-based Healthcare 4.0 framework. To ensure the privacy and integrity of patients' medical records, we will thoroughly review all current rules. Connected to the cloud, Healthcare 4.0 is a state-of-the-art healthcare system that employs smart technology to keep patients monitored in life-threatening scenarios. The Healthcare 4.0 standards include blockchain technology to strengthen data security. In this post, we'll look at how Healthcare 4.0 and other Industry 4.0 security methods are using blockchain technology. A comprehensive comparison of existing approaches is provided by the analyzed findings. Included in the study's conclusion are the main research difficulties and the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: AI in Agriculture: The Future of Robotic Farming and Automation
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: The paper discovers the transformative character of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in recent cultivation, emphasizing its significance in addressing critical challenges and enhancing productivity. It delves into the integration of AI technologies in robotic farming, revolutionizing traditional agricultural practices and increasing efficiency. Additionally, the paper discusses the profound impact of automation on the agricultural industry, from mitigating labor shortages to meeting the increasing demand for food sustainably. Key findings include the probable of AI to augment resource use, recover decision-making, and promote maintainable farming practices. The implications highlight the necessity for continued research, investment, and adoption of AI-driven technologies to ensure the flexibility and sustainability of the agricultural sector in the appearance of global challenges.The paper aims to review various AI techniques (including fuzzy logic, artificial neural networks, genetic algorithms, etc.) in agriculture, focusing on their applications in expert systems, agricultural machines, and sensor technology. It seeks to uncover their potential impact on agriculture, particularly in cultivation, monitoring, and harvesting processes. Despite the extensive literature on AI and robotics in agriculture, there is a deficiency of comprehensive analysis comparing their applications across these key phases. [13]

articleTitle: Overview of Emerging Biological Computational Framework for Olfactory Studies Utilizing Contextual Technobiomedical Engineering
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: Organoid intelligence (OI), the next paradigm of intelligence, draws inspiration from the biological learning of organs. On the other hand, artificial intelligence (AI) draws its inspiration only from the cognitive processes of the brain. While taking ethical and technological limitations into account, biological learning helps to conceptualize, accept, and apply them. Just as AI helped to make supercomputers possible, OI may help create biocomputers. Even though AI has increased the capabilities of technology to unimaginable heights, it still appears immature and is steadily moving toward cognitive computing to push the envelope even farther. In contrast to AI, OI is a new multidisciplinary computer area that attempts to be more approachable. OI has the ability to produce novel biocomputers, such as organoids, that use parts derived from live organisms to perform computational tasks. Organoids, such as human nasal organoids, are microscopic tissue cultures made from stem cells that mimic some of the functions of real organs. Although they have been used for many different purposes, including drug discovery and illness modeling, scientists are only now beginning to explore their potential for biological information processing.

articleTitle: Principle Component Analysis Based Naïve Bayes and K-Nearest Neighbors Classifiers for the Identification of Oral Mucosal Lesions
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: Identification of the oral mucosal lesions has been executed by the machine learning methods in the present study. In the machine learning methods, principle component analysis, naïve Bayes and k-nearest neighbor’s classifiers, and receiver operating characteristic analysis are utilized. PCA is dimension reduction method and employed to reduce the dimension of the fluorescence data. Naïve Bayes is a probabilistic model which is based on the Bayes theorem. KNN is based on distance metric such as Euclidean distances. These methods are adopted for classification among the diseased (cancerous) and non-diseased groups. However, ROC is implemented for the finding of diagnostic parameters like sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy. Data collection was done by the use of fluorescence based portable device. A total of 38 patients (20 OSCC & 18 dysplastic), and 36 healthy volunteers were included in this study. Fluorescence spectral data were recorded from the lateral boarder of tongue (LBT) of the oral cavity. In the spectra, presence of two fluorophores namely FAD and porphyrin were seen. A significant enhancement in the porphyrin fluorescence was noticed on OSCC patients than the volunteers. Data analysis exhibited by the naïve Bayes and KNN classifiers on the testing data differentiated among Normal to OSCC, Normal to Dysplasia, and Dysplasia to OSCC with the accuracy values of 89%, 90%, 88% and 94%, 85%, and 100% respectively. Results indicate that KNN classifier can differentiate the three groups with slightly higher values of accuracy than the naïve Bayes classifier.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence in Enhancing Quality of Education: SEM Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: The study’s overarching goal is to gain a feel for how different types of educators see the potential for AI to improve classroom learning. The fundamental function of artificial intelligence (AI) in attaining a fruitful learning environment is the focus of this investigation. A quantitative research strategy known as an exploratory research design was utilized in the investigation. Students' information is collected from Bangalore city’s Autonomous Institutions. The study’s total sample size was 76 educators, recruited using a convenience sample method. Both SPSS and AMOS were used to analyze the data. The results of the study indicate that teachers have a favorable impression of the ability of AI features to improve academic performance in specific subjects. Educators have found that students' academic performance is greatly improved when they use AI’s collaborative features in conjunction with methods of instruction that go beyond the typical classroom. By including educators' viewpoints in analyzing the effects of AI on subject area education, this study exemplifies methodological innovation. Colleges in Bangalore that are considered independent and have the authority to develop their own curricula with the usage of AI are the subject of this study. Educators' views on AI’s functions and roles are the focus of this study, which hopes to shed light on the topic for educational organizations and policymakers in the field. The stakeholders can classify the functions that aren't contributing anything and decide whether to keep them or eliminate them.

articleTitle: Is AI really improving the quality of digital diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: The research paper shows how AI's application improves the correctness of diagnosis and increases the rate of accomplishing multiple tasks, including when it comes across some hurdles, such as AI-based digital diagnosis algorithms. In the past, AI was used exclusively to process data, work as an analyzing tool for medical images in health information systems, and assist in decision-making. Still, the process often involves deep machine learning. This is an independent work based on the outcome of other research, which indicates that AI increases bias and needs interaction with people.AI has certain privileges over traditional methods, time and again, relating to swift analysis and comprehensive data assimilation. The patient feedback tells us that despite the preference for AI-generated diagnostic hints, people still want a human professional's supervision or confirmation concerning the results achieved in this sphere, which indicates the directions for the further enhancement of AI utilization in healthcare. These comments emphasize the need to continue improving research and development to address concerns regarding data quality, algorithms' explanations, and ethical problems.

articleTitle: AI for Personalized Nutrition and Healthcare Management
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: Personalised nutrition healthcare sectors are rapidly evolving because of the application of artificial intelligence for designing therapies and nutritional recommendations and plans according to personal needs and genetic profiles. Ai is especially versatile at gathering and sculpting data for various sources, including genetic data, microbiome information and Lifestyle elements. This capability allows an AI-driven platform to generate tolerate dietary advice. [1] In the area of healthcare management, the use of AI in studying EHRs and data from wearable devices to identify diseases at an early stage, risk assessment, and personalised treatment plans. AI is useful in improving precision medicine as well as adjusting a drug prescription map and also transforms the paradigms of remote and Telehealth monitoring due to the ability to assess real-time data and virtual conferences. However, problems like data privacy and security and AI algorithm biases remain challenging. Overcoming these issues is critical to maintaining AI’s effectiveness in these areas in the future. The future trends suggest enhancement of the concept of genomics and enhancement of the AI algorithms, signifying a new era in healthcare for addressing the formidable challenges – better health and value efficacy at a lesser cost. Following this brief introduction to AI and the field’s prospective developments and challenges, this article gets to the underlying focus of exploring the role of AI in personalised nutrition/ dietary therapy/ precision medicine and the prospects of the field. [2]

articleTitle: Efficient Detection and Categorization of Thyroid Nodules from Medical Ultrasound Images
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: The use of ML and DL in medical imaging for early illness symptom prediction is substantial. Since 2013, DL has been one of the rising trends in general data analysis. With its multiple hidden layers that allow for a high degree of data abstraction, it is an enhancement of artificial neural networks (ANN). One promising approach for computer vision applications is the use of convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Automatic learning of raw data, particularly photographs, is a capability of deep CNNs. Both the capture and interpretation of images are crucial for the correct diagnosis or evaluation of illness. Devices are able to gather data at a rapid pace with improved resolution because to advancements in image acquisition over the last decade. Nevertheless, computer technology has only just started to improve picture interpretation. Since they are subjective and need highly trained doctors, they are often created by radiologist, physicians, and senior doctors. In medical imaging, computerised tools play a crucial role in facilitating results and improving diagnosis. Early detection and categorization of thyroid nodules by visual inspection and manual study of thyroid ultrasonography (USG) images has traditionally been a tedious process. Identifying benign from malignant thyroid nodules requires manual evaluation of thyroid USG images, which may be a time-consuming and laborious process. The medical industry has seen the emergence of many deep learning models, particularly for the categorization of thyroid nodules, thanks to the growth in processing resources and the fast improvement in technology. Clinical interventions and therapies may be more successful when these nodules are detected early. Thus, a growing number of academics are pushing for the use of computer diagnostic systems (CDS) as a means to statistically and scientifically evaluate USG pictures of thyroid nodules. Creating effective models for identifying and classifying thyroid nodules using ML and DL approaches is the main goal of this effort. In the first stage of this project, two hybrid models, ANN-SVM and CNN-SVM, are suggested.

Author Keywords: Artificial Neural Network-State Vector Machine) ANN-SVM

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning In Autonomous Cars To Preventing Road Accident
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: The integration of autonomous vehicles (AVs) into modern transportation systems presents both unprecedented opportunities and challenges, particularly in ensuring road safety and reducing accidents. This paper explores the application of Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) techniques to enhance decision-making processes in AVs, aiming to proactively prevent road accidents. By simulating complex driving environments, DRL algorithms enable AVs to learn optimal driving strategies through continuous interaction and feedback. We introduce a DRL-based framework that incorporates sensor data fusion, real-time environment analysis, and adaptive control mechanisms. Experimental results from simulated urban and highway scenarios demonstrate a significant reduction in collision rates and improved response to unforeseen obstacles compared to traditional rule-based systems. The findings underscore the potential of DRL in fortifying the reliability and safety of autonomous driving technologies.

articleTitle: Electrical Simulation Systems for Task Specific tremor Suppression : Current Status and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: Tremor is defined by involuntary movements causing part of the body to oscillate. According to the most widely recognized definition, it is "an involuntary, roughly rhythmic, and roughly sinusoidal movement." [1]. The most common movement problem that impairs a patient's the capacity to carry out everyday tasks and engage in physical activities is tremors, which eventually lowers the patient's quality of life. The pathophysiology of tremor makes it difficult to create effective pharmacotherapies, which are only partially successful in managing tremor. Deep brain stimulation is one type of surgical procedure that can effectively decrease tremors over time. However, their use is limited because of their high costs,. In order to deliver safe and efficient tremor suppression, medical devices are the better options to fill the gap between pharmacotherapies and surgical treatments. We examine the operational modes, safety and effectiveness features, and clinical applications of various methods and techniques that are on the market or have been studied in the past for the suppression of Task specific tremorusing Electrical simulation techniques.

articleTitle: Kolmogorov Arnold Network for Hyperspectral Image Classification: A Detailed Explanation
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) has been proved to be useful in numerous fields because of its ability to acquire the spectral information across the hundreds of contiguous bands. Nevertheless, the vast dimensionality of the hyperspectral data presents a great problem especially during data processing as well as during classification. Recently, one of the techniques that have attracted most interest for the classification of hyperspectral images is Kolmogorov Arnold Network (KAN), which is efficient with regard to those high-dimensional non- linear data sets found in hyperspectral imagery. This study focuses on how KAN can be utilized for classifying hyperspectral images, how B-spline curves can be used for augmenting the performance of the model, and what experimentation was done with the state-of-the-art hyperspectral data set. From these results, it was established that KAN plus B-spline curves was a good strategy for hyperspectral images classification compared to existing systems in both accuracy and speed.

articleTitle: Assessing the adoption and impact of AI chatbots in customer service: A survey-based study in Indian service industries
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: This research paper tries to fill a major gap in the available literature by discussing the adoption and impact of chatbots in the service industry in India. Present research is aimed at mapping the level of integration of chatbots into customer service processes in Indian service industries and its impact on customer service quality. The design of research is cross-sectional survey-based. Data have been collected from 200 organizations representing different industries: retail, banking, healthcare, telecommunications, and e-commerce. It undertakes data analysis on IBM SPSS Statistics to analyse the adoption level, challenges, customer satisfaction, and variations within sectors. The key findings of the study are that the adoption rate is high in Indian service industries, with 39.0% of organizations showing complete adoption and 45.0% partial adoption. As many as 60.0% of organizations reported a positive impact of chatbots on customer service quality. Several challenges, like the issue of linguistic diversity and how to handle complex queries, were identified, and upon consideration, made the organizations adopt multilingual chatbots and enhancements in the algorithm for natural language processing. It ranges from variations in the level of chatbot adoption to sectoral level: the highest full adoption rates among the banking organizations and the highest partial adoptions occurred among the healthcare organizations. The higher the level of its adoption, the more satisfied customers are with chatbots. These results, therefore, have practical implications for guiding Indian service industries on the adoption and challenges of chatbots, as well as customer-centric strategies for the same. Further, this study helps plug the gap in the literature by bringing specific insights from the Indian context to the global discussion relating to chatbots and their role in customer service.

articleTitle: A Novel Improved Framework for Speckle Denoising using Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: Ultrasound technology serves as a popular non-invasive diagnostic tool. Speckle noise (SN), a common artifact in ultrasound images can diminish their resolution and contrast potentially affecting the accuracy of disease diagnosis. Researchers have been focused on sophisticated Deep Learning (DL) models to remove simulated additional SN they have not been concentrating on the practical use of DL to remove naturally occurring SN from genuine US images. Mostly DL algorithms used Autoencoder models and CNN based techniques to do so but they experience overfitting, decreased accuracy, and performance deterioration, making it difficult to give enhanced output of ultrasound images. Inspired by the researchers, we proposed Unet-Elu CNN model with Exponential activation function (Elu function). The improved Unet-ELU model consists of 26 layers. Batch normalization, max pooling layers and drop out layers are added for more accuracy and preventing overfitting issue. The objective of this proposed work is to improve the resolution and minimize speckle noise in medical ultrasound images to make images more clear and enhanced for diagnosis of disease. Model has been trained using breast cancer and abdominal dataset, the original US images were given as targets, while the noised US images served as the input. This model was evaluated using the evaluation metrics of PSNR, SSIM, and MSE with different levels of speckle noise in order to determine the effectiveness of these techniques. In comparison with Unet, Leaky relu, CNN Auto-encoder model, and other filtering techniques, proposed framework obtained a PSNR value of 37.76 and SSIM 98%, respectively, indicating better results.

articleTitle: Advancements in Image Captioning using Deep Learning Techniques for Enhanced Descriptive Models
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: Recent improvements in image captioning using deep learning methods have made it much easier to create description models that can correctly understand and describe visual material. Image Captioning is an important part of both computer vision and natural language processing. It involves writing text explanations that match what's in an image. A lot of progress has been made in this area using deep learning models, especially those that use convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to pull out features and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) or transformers to create sequences. Attention mechanisms and other new technologies have made models work better by letting the system focus on certain parts of a image while coming up with words to go with them in the description. Adding transformer-based designs, which are great at managing long-range relationships, has made produced subtitles even better in terms of quality and consistency. These improvements are made possible by transfer learning and big datasets, which help models work better with a wider range of visual material. People are looking into techniques like antagonistic training and reinforcement learning to make the created descriptions flow better and sound more like they were written by a person. Not only do modern image tagging models make labels that are more correct and relevant to the image, they are also more creative and expressive. These improvements can be used in many different ways, from making tools easier for visually impaired people to use to bettering information search systems.

articleTitle: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles and Low-Flying Drones: A Review of Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: Nowadays Research and Development of Novel and Efficient drones becomes the core part of strategic practices of every nation. There is a growing need of using a variety of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles with significant capabilities in Civilian, Military and Commercial Applications. UAVs flight patterns such as Vertical Takeoff Landing and Horizontal Takeoff Landing, its maximum altitude capacity, range are discussed. Designing of Low Flying drones are classified into Small, Micro and Nano-Pico-SmartDust(NPSD) categories. Use and Impact of different materials like Titanium alloy in design is provided. Additionally, current activities in the market related to small drones and future research direction in the field of utility and applications drones are discussed.

articleTitle: A Review on the Developments in the Field of AI-Based Gait Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: The examination of human gait is essential for comprehending motor function, the evolution of diseases, and the effectiveness of rehabilitation in different clinical and research environments. Artificial Intelligence (AI) advancements have recently improved gait analysis methodologies, resulting in increased accuracy, efficiency, and therapeutic effectiveness. This review article compiles the existing literature on AI-based gait analysis. The review emphasizes the role of AI in gait analysis, namely via the use of vision-based approaches, wearable sensor technologies, markerless motion capture systems, and inertial sensor-based methodologies. AI has shown potential in identifying musculoskeletal problems including osteopenia and sarcopenia, forecasting the start of Parkinson's disease, assessing the effects of post-stroke rehabilitation, and diagnosing neurological conditions. In addition, the integration of AI with new technologies such as augmented reality (AR), smart sensors, and wearable devices presents intriguing opportunities to improve gait rehabilitation, enable individualized therapies, and facilitate remote patient monitoring. Although there have been significant breakthroughs, there are still obstacles in creating AI models that can be easily understood for clinical decision-making, establishing standardized procedures for collecting data, and verifying AI algorithms across various populations. This study underlines the transformational potential of AI-based gait analysis in customized healthcare, rehabilitation techniques, and clinical results. In order to fully harness the potential of AI in enhancing human health and well-being, it is imperative to do more research and foster multidisciplinary cooperation.

articleTitle: Leveraging Digital Twin Technology to Combat Cardiovascular Disease: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: The innovative Digital Twin (DT) technology, which constructs a copy of objects, has emerged as a groundbreaking approach in various sectors, including the healthcare industry. This thorough examination delves into the potential of utilizing DT technology to address disease (CVD), a prominent cause of illness and death globally. By combining real-time data, sophisticated analytics and machine learning algorithms, DTs provide a platform for monitoring, diagnosing and enhancing health. The document explores the background and evolution of DT technology, its role in precision medicine, and its transformative impact on managing CVD. It also sheds light on how digital twins replicate, forecast and analyze the functions and performance of systems to offer insights into prevention, therapy options and personalized care. Furthermore, it discusses the obstacles and constraints of incorporating DT technology in healthcare settings, such as data security concerns, interoperability challenges, and ethical considerations. The paper showcases case studies that highlight the applications of DTs in research and treatment to underscore the potential of this technology in transforming patient outcomes. The evaluation concludes with prospects stressing the importance of research efforts and collaborative initiatives to surmount existing hurdles and fully leverage the advantages of DT technology in addressing cardiovascular disease.

articleTitle: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Cost Reduction of Marketing Agencies
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) plays a significant role in optimizing operations, increasing productivity, building more efficiency, and reducing costs across all business verticals of every industry. AI is an essential driver in the field of marketing, fueling creativity and innovations by Automating repetitive tasks, enhanced targeting, personalizing communication, optimizing advertising spending, predictive analytics, Customer Support, and much more. This paper investigates the role of AI in reducing costs for marketing agencies, explicitly focusing on AI tools in content creation, content management, and video editing. Also, AI-powered video editing applications speed up the overall editing process, decreasing reliance on costly software and skilled personnel. Towards the end, the study highlights the practical implications of how marketing agencies can leverage AI tools to develop a more robust and profitable business model that is dynamic to suit the current technology age and drives stability for sustainable growth.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Home Prices
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd DMIHER International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, Education and Industry (IDICAIEI)
abstract: Housing market is a complex structure and is being growing rapidly. The price of any property depends on various factors and to correctly predict the price is a challenging part to perform. This project aims to develop a model which accurately predicts the house prices with the use of machine learning techniques, using a detailed dataset containing various housing features such as location, facilities, environment etc. The methodology consists of data preprocessing, feature engineering and model selection to achieve optimizable outcome. Implementation has been done of algorithms namely Linear regression, decision trees to captured the complex relationships and patterns within the generated predictions. We investigate the relationship between various house attributes and their corresponding selling prices Building a model that can unambiguously estimate the fair market value in case of a house based on a set of relevant features. The training and testing procedures was conducted for accessing the robustness of the model. The outcome not only contains precise predictions but also insights of the housing market dynamics. This project contributes to informed decision-making process for buyers, sellers and real estate professionals too.
